_note: GAM Research forecast drivers for SRF (consolidated, ₹ crore). Segment-driven: each segment's revenue grows and earns an EBITDA margin (segment EBIT + segment depreciation). Group EBITDA = sum of segments less unallocated corporate costs and forex hedge losses (Screener basis). Valued on sum of the parts (EV/EBITDA by segment), as the street does.

segments.name: Chemicals
segments._why: FY27: Q1 +26% on refrigerant volumes and prices; management guides 15-20% and Q2-Q3 are seasonally weaker for refrigerants. We take 19%. FY28: +12% because calendar 2027 is a "free year" before India's HFC quotas, so new capacity can sell and prices may soften; fluoropolymers (PVDF, Chemours FEP/FKM) start to ramp. FY29: +16% as HFOs (Odisha, Q4FY28) and fluoropolymers run for a full year.
segments._marginWhy: Segment EBITDA margin 35.7% in FY26 (EBIT 29.1%); ~33% in Q1FY27 (EBIT 27.6%) as specialty prices stayed under Chinese pressure. We assume no return to FY26's peak: 33.5% / 32.5% / 33.5%.

segments.name: Performance Films & Foil
segments._why: Q1FY27 +42%: the Middle East war shut rival plants and customers panic-bought (management: "an aberration"). We assume Q2-Q4 grow ~10%, so FY27 +18%; FY28 +3% as prices normalise; FY29 +8% from capacitor film, BOPA (Sep-2027), thick BOPET and foil.
segments._marginWhy: EBITDA margin 13.2% in FY26 (EBIT 8.8%); ~20% in Q1FY27 (EBIT 17.3%) including low-cost inventory gains. We assume ~12.5% for Q2-Q4 (FY27 14.9%) and 13.5-14% after.

segments.name: Technical Textiles
segments._why: Q1FY27 +28% (belting exports after US tariff cuts, nylon tyre cord, quality-control order on industrial yarn); Q2-Q4 assumed +8%. Mature business: ~5% a year after.
segments._marginWhy: EBITDA margin 13.4% in FY26; ~20% in Q1FY27 including inventory gains. 14% from FY28 (FY22-26 average ~15%).

_unallocLabel: Unallocated corporate costs and forex hedge losses (reported EBITDA below sum of segments)
_unallocWhy: FY26: ₹434 cr = ₹188 cr forex losses on long-dated export hedges + ₹246 cr corporate costs. Q1FY27 included a ₹102 cr forex loss. FY27E: the Q1 loss plus ~₹100 cr of corporate costs; FY28-29E assume corporate costs only (~₹150 cr) and no further hedge losses.
_capexWhy: FY27 guided ~₹2,500 cr; FY28 carries most of the ₹2,300 cr Odisha HFO plant, BOPA and thick-film lines; Axis expects >₹2,500 cr a year. FY26 actual ₹1,717 cr.
_depWhy: FY26 depreciation ₹852 cr ≈ 4.6% of average gross block; H1FY27 ₹452 cr.
_treasuryWhy: Net debt, so no treasury income; other income entered separately.
_otherIncomeWhy: FY26 other income ₹107 cr before the ₹85 cr Labour Codes exceptional charge; Q1FY27 ₹34 cr.
_interestWhy: FY26 ₹278 cr; Q1FY27 ₹69 cr; debt rising with the capex cycle (₹2,500 cr in FY27).
_taxWhy: Q1FY27 22%; FY26 27% included the exceptional charge; normal ~25%.

dcf._betaWhy: Cyclical chemicals and films; market-like sensitivity.
dcf._tgWhy: Long-run demand for refrigerants, fluoropolymers and films tracks industrial growth; 6% nominal.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: ≈ India nominal GDP less some maturity of HFCs (phase-down) offset by HFOs and fluoropolymers.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex intensity falls from ~10-12% of revenue to ~6% once the HFO / fluoropolymer cycle is done.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: Refrigerant prices hold through the 2027 'free year' and India's 2028 quota freeze; specialty volumes and prices recover with new agro and pharma molecules; HFOs and fluoropolymers ramp on time; films keep a ~14% EBITDA margin.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: HFC prices fall as new capacity sells in 2027; Chinese overcapacity keeps specialty prices down; HFO volumes slip into FY30; films margins revert to the FY24-25 trough.

parts.name: Chemicals
parts.metricLabel: Sep-28E EBITDA (½ FY28E + ½ FY29E) × EV/EBITDA
parts.note: Street after Q1FY27: ICICI Direct 25x and Prabhudas Lilladher 20x (FY28E); Emkay 30x specialty / 18x fluoro; Kotak 18x; Nuvama 25x. 21x = 0.53 × 24x for fluorochemicals (a ~25% discount to Navin Fluorine's ~33x, as SRF's are commodity HFCs) + 0.47 × 18x for specialty (PI Industries), ~20% below SRF's own 26.6x post-2021 median.

parts.name: Performance Films & Foil
parts.note: Street 8-12x (PL 8x, ICICI Direct 10x, Emkay 12x); listed film makers trade at 5-7.5x (Cosmo First 7.5x, Uflex 5.7x, Polyplex 4.8x). 7x = a small premium for SRF's value-added films and foil.

parts.name: Technical Textiles
parts.note: Street 5-8x (ICICI Direct 5x, PL 7x, Emkay 8x). Mature, import-exposed business: 6x.

parts.name: Less: corporate costs
parts.note: Head-office costs not in any segment are real costs; valued at the blended multiple of the businesses (~17x). Brokers leave this out, which flatters their SOTP by ~₹85 a share.

parts.name: Less: net debt at Sep-27E
parts.metricLabel: Net debt at the target date (½ Mar-27E + ½ Mar-28E)
parts.note: Model forecast: borrowings less cash and investments.

methods.name: Sum of the parts
methods.why: How the street values SRF: the brokers that disclose a method after Q1FY27 (ICICI Direct, Prabhudas Lilladher) and earlier (Emkay, Kotak, Nuvama) use segment EV/EBITDA. The four businesses have very different growth and returns, so each needs its own multiple.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: SRF's one-year-forward P/E has a median of ~36x since 2019; at 30-Sep-2026 chemical peers traded 10-25% below their five-year medians (PI Industries 32x vs 38x, Navin Fluorine 53x vs 71x). 36x × ~0.83 ≈ 30x.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 15-year FCFF, Ke 12.5%, terminal growth 6%. Heavy capex keeps free cash flow low for three years.
